newsitem.title: USA: Ceridian age discrimination case opens.
newsitem.headline: Ceridian age discrimination case opens.

text.p: Jury selection began Wednesday in federal court in an age discrimination suit against Ceridian Corp.
The suit was brought by 296 laid-off workers of Control Data Corp., which became Ceridian after the company restructured in 1992.
Officials at the U.S. District Court in Minneapolis said jury selection would probably be completed Wednesday and the trial's opening statements would be aired Thursday.

While class-action status for the case was denied in 1992, the 296 individual suits were consolidated in 1995 into a single suit to determine if a "pattern or practice" of age discrimination occurred during the layoffs. Potential damages are not an issue in the current proceeding, Ceridian said.
If there were a finding against Ceridian, each of the 296 persons would have to prove that he or she was the victim of that discrimination and suffered a financial loss due to it.
Ceridian has denied the charges, saying age had no bearing on the downsizing decisions Control Data made in the 1980s.
Judge John Tunheim of the U.S. District Court will preside over the "pattern or practice" proceeding, which is expected to last six weeks.
